The book already expresses that node via the existing 2027 H-versus-Z curve, and Brent at 102.59 plus a 5.26 percent U.S. 10-year are enough of a near-term inflation offset that expanding Canadian rates or Canada spot tonight is not cleaner. Hold the existing curve; do not chase blocked Australian risk and do not swap into spot Canada against 102-handle oil.

value-guy.invalidation: Stay-flat is wrong if a real-yield, policy, or terms-of-trade clock appears that dates why the 5.26 percent 10-year should converge this session rather than remain a statistical extreme.
value-guy.thesis: The U.S. 10-year at 5.26 is the only rates print with a historical one-year z-score near +3.23, so the rates-first candidate is receive tens, not a two-year United States–Canada spread. That two-year gap is 152 basis points, but the U.S. two-year already screens 99 basis points over SOFR 3.90, so cheap euro or kiwi spot is not a substitute valuation. A one-year yield z-score is not a real-yield or terms-of-trade clock that would start convergence tonight, so the book stays flat.

vol-convexity.thesis: Frozen marks are VIX 16.07, dollar-yen 157.12, dollar-Canada 1.41797, Brent 102.59, and a 5.26 percent U.S. 10-year, with the book flat and no listed options surface. Those are spots and a modest implied-vol print, not a trade. With timing and event risk unspecified, linear spot in foreign exchange, crude, or rates is the wrong instrument because path and gap risk are unbounded while convexity is unmarkable. Hold; do not invent an options overlay and do not endorse a spot substitute.
